Chapter 3: System Analysis

3.1 Existing System & Operational Deficiencies

In typical small-to-medium enterprise and academic IT environments, computing equipment, software entitlements, and employee helpdesk requests are managed using disjointed desktop spreadsheets, paper handovers, and ad-hoc email chains. This approach lacks concurrency controls, automated alerts, and tamper-proof verification, creating severe operational vulnerabilities:

Table 3.1: Operational Deficiencies of the Existing Manual System
Manual System Practice Operational Deficiency & Institutional Risk
Unsynchronized Spreadsheets Multiple administrators edit separate spreadsheet copies, causing conflicting records and duplicate entries.
Untracked Handover Forms Paper issue slips get misplaced, leaving the organization with no legal proof of custody when employees depart.
Manual License Key Tracking License keys exposed in plain text; missed renewal dates cause unexpected service disruption or compliance fines.
Ad-Hoc Email Support Queues Requests lack priority classification and SLA tracking; critical hardware faults languish unassigned in personal inboxes.
Absence of Immutable Audit Trails Modifications, status alterations, and record deletions occur without historical logs, preventing accountability.

3.2 Need for the New System

The development of AssetDesk was motivated by the imperative to establish an automated, secure, and auditable software infrastructure:

  • Single Source of Truth: Eliminate data divergence through an indexed MongoDB database accessed via unified REST endpoints.
  • Custody Accountability: Atomic concurrency guards ensure computing devices are definitively bound to a single employee.
  • Automated License Compliance: Background cron daemons scan software renewal dates daily, proactively triggering visual alerts.
  • Deterministic SLA Enforcement: Dynamic deadline timers enforce transparent ticket resolution across 4 defined status phases.
  • Compliance Audit Journal: Immutable event logging creates cryptographic traceability for every system modification.

3.3 Software Requirements Specification (SRS)

Formulated in accordance with the IEEE-830 standard, system functional and quality requirements define precise behavioral contracts verified by automated integration test suites.

Table 3.2: User Roles & Access Authorization Matrix
User Role System Persona Primary Permissions & Operational Boundary
ADMIN System Administrator Full governance: user creation, asset CRUD, license key reveal, system audit inspection, CSV exports.
IT_SUPPORT Helpdesk Engineer Operational desk: asset status changes, incident triage, resolution notes, and SLA tracking.
EMPLOYEE Standard End-User Self-service: view assigned hardware, submit support tickets, participate in comment threads.

3.3.1 Functional Requirements (Part 1: FR-01 to FR-10)

Req ID Functional Requirement Description Module Priority Test Trace ID
FR-01 User Login: Authenticate users via email & bcrypt hash; issue signed JWT token. M1 Must IT-M1-01
FR-02 Role-Based Access: Restrict endpoints strictly by role (Admin, Support, Employee). M1 Must IT-M1-12
FR-03 User Management: Enable Admin to register staff, modify roles, and toggle active status. M1 Must IT-M1-18
FR-04 Password Change: Authenticated users change passwords upon verifying current hash. M1 Must IT-M1-25
FR-05 Asset Registration: Register physical assets with tag, serial, model, and category. M2 Must IT-M2-01
FR-06 Asset Update: Authorized staff update hardware specs, warranty, and physical location. M2 Should IT-M2-10
FR-07 Asset Assignment: Concurrency-safe atomic allocation of hardware to employees. M2 Must IT-M2-16
FR-08 Lifecycle Transitions: Enforce states: AVAILABLE, ASSIGNED, MAINTENANCE, RETIRED. M2 Must IT-M2-24
FR-09 Asset Audit Filter: Filter inventory by department, status, and assigned custodian. M2 Should IT-M2-31
FR-10 License Tracking: Register software licenses with seat quotas, vendor, and expiry date. M3 Must IT-M3-01

3.3.2 Functional Requirements (Part 2: FR-11 to FR-20)

Req ID Functional Requirement Description Module Priority Test Trace ID
FR-11 Seat Allocation: Allocate license seats preventing over-allocation past total quota. M3 Must IT-M3-05
FR-12 License Expiry Alerts: Proactive alerts for software expiring within 30 days. M3 Must IT-M3-14
FR-13 Ticket Creation: Employees log support incidents with title, category, and priority. M4 Must IT-M4-02
FR-14 SLA Deadline Computation: Dynamic resolution due date based on ticket priority. M4 Should IT-M4-15
FR-15 Ticket State Machine: Linear transitions: OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED. M4 Must IT-M4-22
FR-16 Threaded Comments: Discussion thread between requester and support technician. M4 Should IT-M4-33
FR-17 Audit Logging: Immutable log of timestamp, action, user ID, target entity, and IP. M5 Must IT-M5-01
FR-18 Dashboard KPIs: Real-time aggregates (total assets, active tickets, license seats). M5 Should IT-M5-12
FR-19 CSV Report Export: Export compliant CSV files for assets, licenses, tickets, and audits. M5 Should IT-M5-22
FR-20 License Key Masking: Sensitive software keys masked (XXXX-****-****-XXXX) in UI. M3 Must IT-M3-08

3.3.3 Non-Functional Requirements & Engineering Targets

Quality Attribute Measurable Engineering Target Real Verification Result
Security Encrypted passwords (bcrypt 10 rounds), signed JWT tokens, role guards, Helmet HTTP security headers. 12/12 dedicated security tests passed (SEC-01..12). Injection defense verified.
Performance Query endpoint p95 latency under 100ms; login response time under 250ms for 50 concurrent requests. Measured: POST /auth/login avg 75.82ms; GET /assets avg 7.49ms.
Usability Responsive layout on 1366×768 and 1920×1080 screens; clear form validation errors. 16/16 Playwright system journeys (ST-01..16) validated with automated UI screenshots.
Reliability Zero server crashes during malformed input payloads; uniform JSON error payloads. 100% test pass rate (272/272 tests passing) with 87.16% statement coverage.
